title: Prod: age-check page unstyled + CSRF 403 on submit
description:
Two production-breaking bugs hit on https://switch.berlin/age-check/:

1. **No styling**: page emits <script type=module src=/static/assets/app-cgn4pjPN.css> (a) wrong tag for CSS (django-vite vite_asset renders entries as script regardless of extension), (b) wrong URL — file actually lives at /static/dist/assets/... so whitenoise misses it and LoginWallMiddleware 302s to /accounts/login/. Net effect: no CSS loads on any unauthenticated page.

2. **CSRF 403** on POST /age-check/: SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER is unset, so behind Caddy's TLS termination Django sees request.scheme == http while the Origin header is https://switch.berlin. CsrfViewMiddleware's Origin/Referer check rejects the cross-scheme mismatch.

Repro: open https://switch.berlin/age-check/ in incognito → no styles. Click 'Yes, I am 18+' → 403 CSRF page.
acceptance_criteria: https://switch.berlin/age-check/ loads with full Tailwind/DaisyUI styling (card, btn classes render). Submitting the form with 'Yes, I am 18+' sets age_gate=ok cookie and redirects to / without a 403.
notes: Related: kb-2e3 covers broader prod security hardening (HSTS, SSL redirect, secure cookies). This bead applies only SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER as the minimum needed to unblock CSRF; kb-2e3 stays open for the rest.
close_reason: Deployed in 519ec18: CSS now renders as <link rel=stylesheet> at /static/dist/assets/app-cgn4pjPN.css (200 served by WhiteNoise); POST /age-check/ with valid CSRF returns 302 to / (verified via curl with X-Forwarded-Proto trusted).

title: Build Vite frontend assets during Docker image build
description: The production app container returns HTTP 500 because templates use {% vite_asset %} / {% vite_hmr_client %} (django_vite tags) but static/dist/.vite/manifest.json doesn't exist. The Dockerfile only installs Python deps and runs collectstatic — it never runs the frontend build. Locally devs use Vite's dev server (DJANGO_VITE_DEV_MODE) so the missing manifest is invisible.
design:
## Fix sketch
Multi-stage Dockerfile: add a node:22-slim builder stage that runs npm ci + npm run build in /frontend, then COPY --from=frontend /static/dist into /app/static/dist before collectstatic (so collectstatic picks up the built assets).

## Why P1
Blocks kb-6nq.6 acceptance (A.1 legal pages 200 + h1) — the deploy workflow itself is green but the app cannot serve any HTML view that extends _base.html (which loads vite_asset 'src/app.css').

Verified: (1) docker build local — image has manifest with both entry points (src/app.css, src/events/main.tsx); (2) prod deploy run 25660560062 (commit 116fef3) — green, no django_vite W001 warning; (3) curl https://switch.berlin/ → HTTP 200, h1=Switch (template renders, vite tags resolve); (4) curl https://switch.berlin/static/dist/assets/app-cgn4pjPN.css → HTTP 200, served by Whitenoise via Caddy; (5) /impressum/ → 200; (6) www.switch.berlin → 308 to apex per Caddyfile.

title: Verify production deploy acceptance end-to-end
design:
## Scope

After all other slots are deployed/configured, the full epic acceptance contract (clauses A.1–A.4, B.1–B.5, C.1–C.3) is run as an explicit verification pass against the live production environment.

Each clause's mechanical probe is executed; results are recorded with pass/fail per clause. A clean pass on every clause unblocks closure of the epic. Failures route to the relevant implementation slot for remediation.

This slot is the integration verification gate — it asserts the cross-slot emergent behavior that no individual implementation slot covers in isolation.

Coverage targets: ALL A/B/C clauses (verification, not implementation).
acceptance_criteria:
All thirteen clauses of the epic's A/B/C acceptance contract are executed against the live production environment in a single verification pass, and each clause is recorded as pass or fail before this slot is closed.

**External probes:** All four public URLs return HTTP 200 with the expected heading (A.1); at least one referenced static asset per page returns 200 with a matching Content-Type (A.2); the TLS certificate issuer Organisation reads "Let's Encrypt" (A.3); a request to the www subdomain is redirected to the apex domain with a 301 or 308 status (A.4).

**On-host probes:** The migration check exits 0 (B.1); the deployment configuration check exits 0 (B.2); all four expected service containers are reported running and healthy (B.3); the backup timer's last-triggered timestamp is non-empty (B.4); a restic restore into an isolated scratch container produces a row count or schema checksum matching the source database (B.5).

**Gate posture:** The impressum contact address is confirmed as the designated protonmail address (C.1); the public-read flag is enabled and its origin is traced to the seeding migration, not a manual set (C.2); the deployment check exits 0 confirming the env-var population gate is satisfied (C.3).

**Verification record:** A pass/fail result is recorded per clause code (A.1 through C.3). Any failing clause routes to the relevant implementation slot for remediation; the epic is unblocked only when all thirteen clauses record pass.

title: Implement GH Actions deploy workflow
design:
## Scope

A GitHub Actions workflow exists in the repository at `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` that triggers on push to `main` and executes the D4 ordered steps end-to-end:

1. SSH into the VPS as the deploy user and pull `main` into the working directory.
2. Render `/opt/switch-berlin/.env` from GH Actions Secrets and non-secret workflow env (mode 600, owned by deploy user) — must complete before any compose invocation.
3. `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file /opt/switch-berlin/.env build app`.
4. `docker compose ... up -d --remove-orphans`.
5. `docker compose exec app python manage.py migrate --no-input` (apply pending migrations).
6. `docker compose exec app python manage.py migrate --check` (post-condition: exit 0 means no migrations pending).
7. `docker compose exec app python manage.py check --deploy` (blocking: fails workflow if non-zero).
8. `systemctl start kb-backup.service` to populate the timer's `LAST` column on first deploy.

A failed step short-circuits the workflow.

Coverage targets: A.1 (legal pages 200 + h1 — workflow brings app live), A.2 (static assets serve), B.1 (migrate --check exit 0), B.2 (check --deploy exit 0), B.3 (compose ps healthy), B.4 partial (workflow step 8 starts kb-backup.service), C.3 partial (workflow consumes slot-4 secrets and runs check --deploy).
acceptance_criteria:
A `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` file targeting the `main` branch is present in the repository.

A push to `main` produces a completed GH Actions workflow run with status "success" (no step exits non-zero, no step is skipped due to a prior failure).

At the conclusion of a green workflow run, all four compose services are observed as running or healthy on the VPS — verifiable via `docker compose ps` without manual intervention.

At the conclusion of a green workflow run, `manage.py migrate --check` exits 0 on the deployed container, confirming no pending migrations remain.

At the conclusion of a green workflow run, `manage.py check --deploy` exits 0 on the deployed container, confirming all required environment variables (including `IMPRESSUM_*`) are populated and the deployment system check is satisfied.
notes:
## ADRs consulted
- docs/decisions/ADR-001-core-product-and-stack.md
- docs/decisions/ADR-002-phased-rollout-and-legal-gate.md
- docs/decisions/ADR-006-legal-gate-execution.md

title: Provision backup subsystem on VPS (restic to Hetzner Storage Box)
design:
## Scope

A `kb-backup.service` systemd unit and `kb-backup.timer` exist on the VPS. The service performs `pg_dump` of the production Postgres container piped through `restic backup` to a Hetzner Storage Box repository. The timer is enabled at boot and scheduled nightly. The restic repository is initialized at the Storage Box destination (one-time bootstrap).

The service can be triggered manually via `systemctl start kb-backup.service`; the timer's `LAST` column populates after the first triggered run. Backup integrity is verifiable: the latest restic snapshot restores into a scratch container with `events_event` row count matching live ±1 if non-empty, or `pg_dump --schema-only` checksum matching live if empty.

Slot-3 owns the subsystem (units installed + timer enabled + restic repo initialized + manual run produces a verifiable snapshot). The first-deploy auto-trigger that populates the timer's `LAST` column is slot-5's workflow responsibility (avoids circular dep).

Coverage targets: B.4 (timer enabled + scheduled + LAST populated post-trigger), B.5 (restic snapshot restores).
acceptance_criteria:
The backup timer unit is reported as enabled by the system init manager, and when queried for scheduled state it shows a future NEXT trigger time.

A manual one-shot trigger of the backup service completes without error and leaves at least one snapshot visible in the restic repository at the Hetzner Storage Box destination.

The restic repository at the Storage Box destination is in an initialized state prior to any service run, confirmed by a snapshot-listing command returning successfully with zero snapshots and no initialization error.

A snapshot produced by a manual trigger is restorable into an isolated scratch context: if the live database contains rows in the events table, the restored row count matches the live count within one row; if the live database is empty, a schema-only export from the restored database produces a checksum identical to the same export from the live database.
notes:
## ADRs consulted
- docs/decisions/ADR-001-core-product-and-stack.md
- docs/decisions/ADR-002-phased-rollout-and-legal-gate.md
- docs/decisions/ADR-006-legal-gate-execution.md

Manual trigger on empty stack → snapshot 6790673b (marker). title: Create docker-compose.prod.yml production overlay
design:
## Scope

A `docker-compose.prod.yml` overlay file exists in the repository. It adds `restart: unless-stopped` to all four services (`app`, `qcluster`, `bot`, `db`); declares host-bind-mount paths under `/opt/switch-berlin/` for the database volume; applies production resource limits where appropriate. It does NOT add or override services.

The base `docker-compose.yml` remains dev-safe; the prod overlay is composable with it. The production image, when built via this overlay, includes collected static assets per D7 (Whitenoise serves them; no runtime collectstatic needed).

This slot is a pure repo artifact — verifiable locally without a live VPS.

title: Provision Hetzner VPS, DNS, and Caddy TLS reverse proxy
design:
## Scope

A live Hetzner Cloud VPS in an EU region (Falkenstein or Nuremberg) is reachable on the public internet at `switch.berlin` and `www.switch.berlin`. Caddy is installed on the host and configured to terminate TLS via Let's Encrypt for both apex and `www`, with `www` redirecting to apex via 301/308. Caddy reverse-proxies application traffic to the compose stack (proxy upstream configured but app not yet running). The deploy user account and working directory `/opt/switch-berlin/` exist on the host. The `switch.berlin` domain's A/AAAA records at inwx point at the VPS public IP.

This slot delivers reachable infrastructure only — the application containers are not started here; that is slot-5's responsibility.

Coverage targets: A.3 (TLS issuer Let's Encrypt), A.4 (www→apex redirect), supporting infrastructure for B.3.
acceptance_criteria:
A DNS resolution of `switch.berlin` and `www.switch.berlin` each returns the VPS public IP address via an A record (IPv4) and/or AAAA record (IPv6).

When a TLS handshake is performed against `switch.berlin:443`, the certificate issuer Organisation field is `Let's Encrypt`.

An HTTPS request to any path under `https://www.switch.berlin/` receives a 301 or 308 redirect response pointing to the corresponding `https://switch.berlin/` URL; port 80 on either host responds with a redirect to HTTPS.

The VPS host contains an OS user account designated for deployments and the directory `/opt/switch-berlin/` exists and is owned by that account.
notes:
ACCEPTANCE PROBES (all green, run from laptop, post-DNS-propagation):

- dig +short switch.berlin A → 128.140.56.30 ✓
- dig +short switch.berlin AAAA → 2a01:4f8:c014:7cbc::1 ✓
- dig +short www.switch.berlin {A,AAAA} → same IPs ✓
- openssl s_client | openssl x509 -noout -issuer → 'O = Let'\''s Encrypt' (CN=E7) ✓
- curl -sI https://www.switch.berlin/ → 308 → https://switch.berlin/ ✓
- curl -sI http://switch.berlin/ → 308 (HTTP→HTTPS) ✓
- ssh switch@host 'stat -c %U /opt/switch-berlin' → switch ✓
- (apex returns 502 from / because no app upstream yet — kb-6nq.5; TLS still terminates correctly)

DEPLOYMENT GAP DISCOVERED + FIXED:
The 'caddy' debian package's postinst did NOT create the system user/group on Ubuntu 24.04 (status=217/USER). cloud-init.yaml updated with explicit groupadd/useradd block before package install loop. Future VPS rebuilds via this cloud-init will provision Caddy correctly without the manual fix-up.

DNS panel: Cloudflare (DNS-only / grey-cloud). Updated via API in /tmp/cf_dns_setup.py (token loaded from .env). 4 records: A/AAAA × @/www, all proxied=False.
close_reason: All 4 acceptance probes pass: DNS resolves to VPS, TLS issuer = Let's Encrypt, www→apex 308, /opt/switch-berlin owned by deploy user. Caddy user-creation gap fixed in cloud-init.yaml for re-provisioning.

title: Organizer LIA doc + consent_method migration to legitimate_interest
description:
Write the Legitimate Interests Assessment doc for organizer data and migrate Organizer.consent_method to the new legal basis per ADR-006 D2 (FIRM). Organizer event data is processed under Art. 6(1)(f) LI, not implied consent.

FILES:
- Create: docs/compliance/organizer-lia.md
- Modify: organizers/models.py
- Create: organizers/migrations/0NNN_add_legitimate_interest_choice.py
- Create: organizers/migrations/0NNN_backfill_consent_method.py (data migration)
- Create: tests/test_organizer_lia_migration.py

LIA DOCUMENT (docs/compliance/organizer-lia.md) must contain:
  1. Purpose: curate public listings of Berlin queer/kink events sourced from public Telegram channels and Instagram.
  2. Necessity: no less-intrusive alternative; events are already public on source channels; we add discoverability, not new exposure.
  3. Balancing: organizers are semi-public figures acting in a public capacity; no special-category data about the organizer is processed; the opt-out path (/takedown/) is accessible without login and responds within 72h.
  4. Art. 21 opt-out path: reference the /takedown/ endpoint; describe the outcome (organizer listing hidden within 72h; event ingestion halted for that source).
  5. Review trigger: re-assess if 3+ organizer objections per quarter.

SCHEMA CHANGE (organizers/models.py):
  Current choices for consent_method:
    ("telegram_forward_implied", "Telegram forward (implied)")
  Add before existing:
    ("legitimate_interest", "Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f))")

  Full new choices list:
    CONSENT_METHOD_CHOICES = [
        ("legitimate_interest", "Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f))"),
        ("telegram_forward_implied", "Telegram forward (implied)"),
    ]

SCHEMA MIGRATION: standard Django migration to add the new choice (no DB column change, just choices kwarg update for documentation/admin dropdown).

DATA MIGRATION (separate migration file):
  from django.db import migrations

  def backfill_consent_method(apps, schema_editor):
      Organizer = apps.get_model("organizers", "Organizer")
      for org in Organizer.objects.filter(consent_method="telegram_forward_implied"):
          org.consent_method = "legitimate_interest"
          existing_notes = org.consent_notes or ""
          org.consent_notes = existing_notes + "\nMigrated to Art. 6(1)(f) per ADR-006 on 2026-04-22."
          org.save(update_fields=["consent_method", "consent_notes"])

  def reverse_backfill(apps, schema_editor):
      Organizer = apps.get_model("organizers", "Organizer")
      for org in Organizer.objects.filter(consent_method="legitimate_interest"):
          org.consent_method = "telegram_forward_implied"
          org.save(update_fields=["consent_method"])

  class Migration(migrations.Migration):
      dependencies = [("organizers", "0NNN_add_legitimate_interest_choice")]
      operations = [migrations.RunPython(backfill_consent_method, reverse_backfill)]

TESTS (tests/test_organizer_lia_migration.py):
  - After running migration forward: all previously telegram_forward_implied rows now have consent_method="legitimate_interest" and consent_notes contains "ADR-006"
  - Running migration twice (idempotency): rows not double-migrated; consent_notes not duplicated
  - Admin organizer change form shows "Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f))" in dropdown
  - docs/compliance/organizer-lia.md exists and contains the words "Art. 6(1)(f)", "balancing", "takedown"

  from django.core.checks import Error, Warning, register
  REQUIRED_LEGAL_VARS = ['IMPRESSUM_NAME', 'IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS', 'IMPRESSUM_EMAIL']

  @register()
  def check_legal_contact(app_configs, **kwargs):
      from django.conf import settings
      from a_core.models import get_flag
      errors = []
      public_read = get_flag('PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED', default=False)
      missing = [v for v in REQUIRED_LEGAL_VARS if not getattr(settings, v, '')]
      if not missing:
          return errors
      if public_read:
          errors.append(Error(
              'PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True but required legal env vars are empty: ' + ', '.join(missing),
              hint='Set IMPRESSUM_NAME, IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS, IMPRESSUM_EMAIL in your environment.',
              obj=settings,
              id='a_core.E006',

              hint='Fill before setting PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True.',

title: step-8a: Rate limiting on write endpoints
description:
Design: /workspace/docs/plans/2026-04-21-bundle-a-post-0.5-code-sprint-design.md#in-10-infra

Depends on: step-1 (unified cache infrastructure in place). ADR-004 D3: block=False + error partial for all 429s (no bare 429 page).

Replaces the existing hand-rolled FLAG_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER=10 constant and its test. Extends django-ratelimit (already imported at /workspace/reviews/views.py line 10) to all write endpoints using block=False + request.limited pattern.

## Current state (before this bead)
- /workspace/reviews/views.py line 20: FLAG_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER = 10
- /workspace/reviews/views.py lines 121-135: hand-rolled daily count check using Flag.objects.filter(reporter=...).count()
- /workspace/reviews/views.py line 265: @ratelimit(key='ip', rate='3/h', method='POST', block=False) on organizer_opt_out_view (NOT takedown_view; takedown uses is_ratelimited inline at line 172)
- /workspace/reviews/test_flags.py line 713: test_flag_target_rate_limit_per_day (tests the hand-rolled logic)
- RATELIMIT_ENABLE setting does NOT currently exist in /workspace/a_core/settings.py — add it

## Changes required

### 1. Staff bypass key function — define once in /workspace/reviews/views.py
Place near the top of the file, after existing imports, before the first view:
  def _user_rate_key(group, request):
      """Rate-limit key function: returns user PK as string, or None for staff (bypass)."""
      if not request.user.is_authenticated:
          return str(request.META.get('REMOTE_ADDR', 'anon'))
      return None if request.user.is_staff else str(request.user.pk)

This exact callable signature matches django-ratelimit's key= parameter for custom functions: (group: str, request: HttpRequest) -> str | None. Returning None disables rate-limiting for that request.

### 2. Flag submission rewrite in /workspace/reviews/views.py
Remove FLAG_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER = 10 from line 20.
Add from django_ratelimit.core import is_ratelimited (django_ratelimit.decorators.ratelimit already imported at line 10).
Add from django.utils.translation import gettext as _ if not present.

In flag_target view, replace the hand-rolled block (lines 121-135) with:
  limited_hourly = is_ratelimited(request, fn=flag_target, key=_user_rate_key, rate='5/h', method='POST', increment=True)
  limited_daily = is_ratelimited(request, fn=flag_target, key=_user_rate_key, rate='20/d', method='POST', increment=True)
  if limited_hourly or limited_daily:
      return render(request, 'reviews/_flag_button.html',
                    {'error': _('Rate limit reached, try again later.')}, status=429)

Error partial: /workspace/templates/reviews/_flag_button.html (confirmed exists, renders {{ error }} at line 4).

### 3. Review submission rate limit in submit_review view
After RATINGS_ENABLED check (line ~36), add:
  if is_ratelimited(request, fn=submit_review, key=_user_rate_key, rate='10/d', method='POST', increment=True):
      return render(request, 'reviews/_rating_form.html',
                    {'error': _('Rate limit reached, try again later.')}, status=429)

Error partial: /workspace/templates/reviews/_rating_form.html (confirmed exists, renders {{ error }} at line 4).

### 4. Signup rate limit via allauth SignupView override
The signup flow uses allauth's NoSignupAdapter (at /workspace/accounts/adapter.py). Allauth's signup view URL is /accounts/signup/ (routed via path('accounts/', include('allauth.urls'))). There is currently no custom SignupView in /workspace/accounts/views.py.

Override allauth's SignupView in /workspace/accounts/views.py:
  from allauth.account.views import SignupView
  from django_ratelimit.core import is_ratelimited
  from django.shortcuts import render
  from django.utils.translation import gettext as _

  class RateLimitedSignupView(SignupView):
      def post(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
          if is_ratelimited(request, fn=self.post, key='ip', rate='3/h', method='POST', increment=True):
              return render(request, 'account/signup.html',
                            {'error': _('Too many signup attempts. Try again later.')}, status=429)
          return super().post(request, *args, **kwargs)

Register in /workspace/a_core/urls.py — replace 'path("accounts/", include("allauth.urls"))' with individual URL overrides, OR add the custom view BEFORE the allauth include:
  from accounts.views import RateLimitedSignupView
  path('accounts/signup/', RateLimitedSignupView.as_view(), name='account_signup'),
  path('accounts/', include('allauth.urls')),

The custom path must come before the allauth.urls include so Django's URL resolver matches it first.

### 5. Takedown bump in /workspace/reviews/views.py (lines 169-184)
Change existing rate='5/h' to rate='10/h'. The is_ratelimited call is at line 172 (inline, no decorator). Change the rate kwarg only.

Note: takedown_view uses key='ip' (anonymous form). No change to key function needed here.

### 6. RATELIMIT_ENABLE kill-switch in /workspace/a_core/settings.py
Add near the existing ratelimit import area (or at the end of settings):
  RATELIMIT_ENABLE = env.bool('RATELIMIT_ENABLE', default=True)
This is django-ratelimit's built-in setting name — setting it False disables all rate limits instantly (no cache lag; requires env reload).

### 7. Delete old test and add new tests
Delete test at /workspace/reviews/test_flags.py line 713 (test_flag_target_rate_limit_per_day) — it tests the hand-rolled logic that no longer exists, and it imports FLAG_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER from reviews.views which will be removed.
Add new tests using override_settings(RATELIMIT_ENABLE=True) and django.test.RequestFactory or Client:
  - 6th flag POST in same hour from same user → 429 with _flag_button.html content
  - 21st flag POST in same day from same user → 429 with _flag_button.html content
  - Staff user: 100 flag POSTs succeed (_user_rate_key returns None for staff → no bucket)
  - 11th review POST in same day → 429 with _rating_form.html content
  Note: use override_settings(RATELIMIT_ENABLE=True) in rate limit tests to ensure limits are active in test environment.

## Key files
- /workspace/reviews/views.py (flag_target rewrite lines 20+121-135; submit_review rate limit; takedown bump line ~172; _user_rate_key function)
- /workspace/reviews/test_flags.py (delete test at line 713; add new django-ratelimit tests)
- /workspace/accounts/views.py (add RateLimitedSignupView class)
- /workspace/a_core/urls.py (add custom signup path before allauth.urls include)
- /workspace/a_core/settings.py (add RATELIMIT_ENABLE setting)

## Acceptance Criteria
- 6th flag POST in same hour → 429 with rendered _flag_button.html error partial (not bare response)
- 21st flag POST in same day → 429 with rendered error partial
- 11th review POST in same day → 429 with rendered _rating_form.html error partial
- 4th signup attempt from same IP in same hour → 429
- Staff user: 100 flag POSTs succeed
- FLAG_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER constant no longer exists in reviews/views.py
- test_flag_target_rate_limit_per_day deleted; new django-ratelimit tests pass
- RATELIMIT_ENABLE=False in env disables all limits (test with override_settings)

## Verification

  uv run pytest reviews/tests.py -x -k 'rate'
  uv run pytest accounts/tests.py -x -k 'signup'

title: step-3: finalize_attendance task + recompute_aggregates extension
description:
Design: /workspace/docs/plans/2026-04-21-bundle-a-post-0.5-code-sprint-design.md#background-tasks

Bundled together to prevent attendance_count=0 regression. Must ship atomically: the nightly that flips 'going'->'went' would zero out all past event attendance_counts without the recompute fix. ADR-002 D1 applies.

## Changes required

### 1. New django-q2 task: finalize_attendance
Add to /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py (same file as recompute_aggregates):

  def finalize_attendance():
      import logfire
      import time
      from django.utils import timezone
      from datetime import timedelta
      from events.models import Attendance, Event
      t0 = time.monotonic()
      cutoff = timezone.now() - timedelta(hours=24)
      past_events = Event.objects.filter(
          status='published', hidden=False,
          end__isnull=False, end__lt=cutoff,
      )
      updated = Attendance.objects.filter(
          event__in=past_events, status='going',
      ).update(status='went')
      duration_ms = int((time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000)
      logfire.info('finalize_attendance.done', updated_count=updated, duration_ms=duration_ms)

Skips events with end=None (intentional: no-end-time events stay going indefinitely).
Skips cancelled events (filter is status='published').
A zero-count run with no exception still logs (updated_count=0, duration_ms measured).

### 2. Register in /workspace/ingestion/management/commands/schedule_tasks.py
Existing tasks use Schedule.DAILY. Add a third using Schedule.CRON for time-of-day control:

  Schedule.objects.update_or_create(
      name='nightly_finalize_attendance',
      defaults={
          'func': 'ingestion.tasks_flags.finalize_attendance',
          'schedule_type': Schedule.CRON,
          'cron': '0 2 * * *',
          'repeats': -1,
      },
  )

Note: django-q2 Schedule has no timezone kwarg; cron runs in UTC.
'0 2 * * *' = 02:00 UTC = 03:00 Europe/Berlin CET = 04:00 CEST.
Add a comment in schedule_tasks.py explaining the UTC offset so future maintainers don't break DST.

### 3. Extend recompute_aggregates in /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py line 66
Current line 66:
  going = Attendance.objects.filter(event=event, status='going').count()

Change to:
  going_or_went = Attendance.objects.filter(event=event, status__in=('going', 'went')).count()

Update line 70 to use going_or_went instead of going for attendance_count.

Also add at end of recompute_aggregates (after the event loop), using time.monotonic() for duration:
  logfire.info('recompute_aggregates.done', event_count=Event.objects.count(), duration_ms=int((time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000))

Add t0 = time.monotonic() at the start of recompute_aggregates.

## Backfill note (no separate step needed)
There is no separate backfill step. The updated recompute_aggregates naturally self-heals on its first nightly run after landing: it will count status='going' AND status='went' for all events, including any past events whose attendees were previously finalized. Any existing going->went transitions that happened before this bead lands will be picked up on the next recompute run. This is intentional and idempotent — the recompute task regenerates all counts from scratch each run, so there is no risk of double-counting.

## Key files
- /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py (add finalize_attendance; update recompute_aggregates lines 66 and 70)
- /workspace/ingestion/management/commands/schedule_tasks.py (add Schedule.CRON entry)
- /workspace/events/models.py (Attendance.status choices include 'went' at line 143 — no change needed)
- /workspace/ingestion/tests/ (add tests: test_finalize_attendance_flips_going_to_went, test_finalize_skips_no_end_events, test_recompute_after_finalize_preserves_count)

## Acceptance Criteria
- finalize_attendance flips Attendance(status='going') to 'went' for events with end < now()-24h, status='published', hidden=False
- Events with end=None stay at 'going'
- Events with Event.status='cancelled' are skipped
- After finalize_attendance then recompute_aggregates: past event with 3 going attendees has attendance_count==3 not 0
- finalize_attendance emits logfire.info('finalize_attendance.done', updated_count=N, duration_ms=N) — both fields required
- recompute_aggregates emits logfire.info('recompute_aggregates.done', event_count=N, duration_ms=N) — both fields required
- Zero-count run still logs (updated_count=0 with duration_ms measured)
- Schedule entry 'nightly_finalize_attendance' appears after running schedule_tasks

## Verification
  uv run pytest ingestion/tests/ -x -k 'finalize'
  uv run pytest ingestion/tests/ -x -k 'recompute'
  uv run python manage.py schedule_tasks

title: step-1: Schema + config + first consumer
description:
Design: /workspace/docs/plans/2026-04-21-bundle-a-post-0.5-code-sprint-design.md#data-model-deltas

Ships four schema changes + unified whole-row cache + data migration + first call-site replacement in one bead to prevent dead-code antipattern.

## Changes required

### 1. New model: a_core.ModerationAction
Add to /workspace/a_core/models.py:

  class ModerationAction(models.Model):
      moderator = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
      flag = models.ForeignKey('reviews.Flag', null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL)
      target_type = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=[
          ('event','Event'),('organizer','Organizer'),('review','Review')
      ])
      target_id = models.IntegerField()
      target_repr = models.CharField(max_length=200,
          help_text='Snapshot of target label at action time; preserved after deletion')
      action = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=[
          ('no_action','No action'),('hide','Hide target'),
          ('delete','Delete review (soft)'),('suspend','Suspend organizer'),('resolved','Mark resolved')
      ])
      reason = models.TextField(blank=True)
      created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
      class Meta:
          indexes = [models.Index(fields=['target_type','target_id'])]

### 2. New field: reviews.Review.hidden
Add to /workspace/reviews/models.py, inside class Review(models.Model):
  hidden = models.BooleanField(default=False, db_index=True)

All existing Review.objects display queries must filter hidden=False after this migration.

### 3. Extended model: a_core.FeatureFlag.numeric_value
Add to FeatureFlag in /workspace/a_core/models.py:
  numeric_value = models.IntegerField(null=True, blank=True,
      help_text='For threshold-style flags; None means boolean-only')

### 4. New field: events.Event.avg_rating
Add to Event in /workspace/events/models.py (alongside existing rating_count at line 90):
  avg_rating = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)

Update recompute_aggregates in /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py to compute avg_rating for events:
  from django.db.models import Avg
  avg = Review.objects.filter(event=event).aggregate(avg=Avg('rating'))['avg']
  Event.objects.filter(pk=event.pk).update(
      attendance_count=...,
      interested_count=...,
      rating_count=rating_count,
      avg_rating=avg,
  )

This field is required by step-7a (event star chip) which uses event.avg_rating. Confirmed: Event currently has rating_count (line 90) but no avg_rating field.

### 5. Unified whole-row cache + get_numeric helper
CURRENT state: cache key is 'feature_flag:{key}', stores only the boolean .enabled value (see /workspace/a_core/models.py lines 20-25 and 48-55).

CHANGE: migrate to 'feature_flag_row:{key}' which stores the entire FeatureFlag model instance (pickle-serialized by Django's cache framework — standard behavior). Both get_flag and get_numeric project from this single cached row.

In /workspace/a_core/models.py:

  a) FeatureFlag.save() line 20: change cache.delete('feature_flag:{self.key}') to cache.delete('feature_flag_row:{self.key}')
  b) FeatureFlag.delete() line 24: change cache.delete('feature_flag:{key}') to cache.delete('feature_flag_row:{key}')
  c) Rewrite get_flag() (lines 46-56) to project .enabled from cached row.
     The stored value changes from bool to a FeatureFlag model instance:
       def get_flag(key: str, default: bool = False) -> bool:
           cache_key = f'feature_flag_row:{key}'
           row = cache.get(cache_key)
           if row is None:
               try:
                   row = FeatureFlag.objects.get(key=key)
                   cache.set(cache_key, row, timeout=60)
               except FeatureFlag.DoesNotExist:
                   return default
           return row.enabled
  d) Add new function get_numeric():
       def get_numeric(key: str, default: int) -> int:
           cache_key = f'feature_flag_row:{key}'
           row = cache.get(cache_key)
           if row is None:
               try:
                   row = FeatureFlag.objects.get(key=key)
                   cache.set(cache_key, row, timeout=60)
               except FeatureFlag.DoesNotExist:
                   return default
           if row.numeric_value is None:
               return default
           return row.numeric_value

Cache stale-key note: After deploy, old 'feature_flag:{key}' entries naturally expire within 60s TTL — no manual cache-bust needed. Both old and new keys coexist briefly during this window; the new code only reads 'feature_flag_row:{key}', so there is no split-brain risk post-deploy.

NOTE: MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY (line 18 of reviews/views.py, imported at organizers/views.py line 8) is NOT replaced in this step. Only AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD is replaced now. MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY will be replaced when step-4 upgrades the organizer reviews UI (step-4 will add get_numeric('threshold.organizer_ratings_display', default=3) and update organizers/views.py). Do not remove MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY in this step.

### 6. Data migration seeding 8 new flag rows
Migration numbering (based on existing migrations):
  - a_core: existing 0001, 0002, 0003 → create 0004_featureflag_numeric_value_moderationaction (schema) + 0005_seed_bundle_a_flags (data)
  - reviews: existing 0001, 0002, 0003 → create 0004_review_hidden (schema)
  - events: existing 0001–0005 → create 0006_event_avg_rating (schema)

Create /workspace/a_core/migrations/0005_seed_bundle_a_flags.py. Must depend on 0004 AND on ('a_core', '0003_seed_featureflags'). Uses get_or_create with defaults to preserve admin-flipped values on re-run.

New rows to seed (the 6 original rows from 0003_seed_featureflags.py are NOT re-seeded here):
  - threshold.organizer_ratings_display: numeric_value=3, enabled=True
  - threshold.event_ratings_display: numeric_value=3, enabled=True
  - threshold.auto_hide_flag: numeric_value=3, enabled=True
  - threshold.attendance_display: numeric_value=5, enabled=True
  - threshold.follower_display: numeric_value=5, enabled=True
  - EVENT_REVIEWS_DISPLAYED: enabled=False
  - TRENDING_SORT_ENABLED: enabled=True
  - INGESTION_PAUSED: enabled=False

### 7. First consumer: replace AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD in /workspace/reviews/views.py
  - Line 19: remove 'AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD = 3'
  - Add 'from a_core.models import get_numeric' to imports
  - Line 148: replace 'if auth_flag_count >= AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD:' with 'if auth_flag_count >= get_numeric("threshold.auto_hide_flag", default=3):'
  - Line 157: same replacement (second call site in organizer branch)

## Key files
- /workspace/a_core/models.py (ModerationAction, FeatureFlag.numeric_value, unified cache, get_numeric)
- /workspace/a_core/migrations/0004_featureflag_numeric_value_moderationaction.py (schema migration)
- /workspace/a_core/migrations/0005_seed_bundle_a_flags.py (data migration)
- /workspace/reviews/models.py (Review.hidden field)
- /workspace/reviews/migrations/0004_review_hidden.py (schema migration)
- /workspace/events/models.py (add Event.avg_rating field)
- /workspace/events/migrations/0006_event_avg_rating.py (schema migration)
- /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py (update recompute_aggregates to compute Event.avg_rating)
- /workspace/reviews/views.py (remove AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD at line 19; add get_numeric at lines 148+157)

## Acceptance Criteria
- uv run python manage.py migrate runs without error
- get_flag and get_numeric on same key project from unified cache (cache key 'feature_flag_row:{key}', stores full FeatureFlag instance)
- All 8 new flag rows exist in DB after migration
- Event.avg_rating field exists and recompute_aggregates populates it
- reviews/views.py contains no AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD constant
- MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY still exists in reviews/views.py (not replaced in this step)
- After deploy, stale 'feature_flag:{key}' cache entries expire naturally within 60s TTL — no manual cache-bust required (document this in migration PR description)

## Verification
  uv run pytest a_core/tests.py -x
  uv run pytest reviews/tests.py reviews/test_flags.py -x
  uv run python manage.py migrate

title: Refactor syndication schema: add PlatformConnection, refront projection FK, add provenance + attribution fields
design:
## Context

The C3/C5 authoring-UX brainstorm (2026-05-26) refined ADR-016 D2 and added D4/D5. The as-built C1 schema (`syndication/models.py`, kb-a4u.1, closed 2026-05-26) predates these: it shipped `PlatformProjection.platform_id` as a `CharField` (with `'telegram-channel:<id>'` string-encoding) and has no `PlatformConnection` model, no `provenance`, and no agent-attribution reservation fields. This bead aligns the schema to the evolved ADR. Pre-launch, so a squashable migration per ADR-008 D1 (no backward-compat shim).

## Decisions (all canonical in ADR-016 D2/D4 — this bead implements, does not re-decide)

1. **Add `PlatformConnection` model** (per ADR-016 D4) — a specific syndication destination owned by an organizer. Fields: organizer/Profile FK (ADR-007 D2), `platform`, destination identifier, per-destination credentials, `enabled` flag, supported `kinds` (Switch page=listing, Ticket Tailor=listing, Telegram=promotion, FetLife=both). An organizer may hold multiple connections per platform. This model is simultaneously the organizer's syndication-targets setting and the per-organizer adapter credential store the adapter beads (kb-a4u.10–.16) consume.
2. **Refront `PlatformProjection.platform_id` → `connection` FK** to `PlatformConnection`. Remove the `platform_id` string.
3. **Add `provenance`** enum field ∈ {`rule_template`, `agent_supplied`, `manual`} (per ADR-016 D2 refinement) — flips to `manual` on human edit of an override.
4. **Add ADR-003 reservation fields** `generated_by` (nullable agent identity ref) + `last_generated_at` (nullable datetime). Empty for human-driven flows; the columns a future `ProjectionRevision` history table would key on.
5. Retain the existing `override_data` JSONField (effective content = live canonical + override_data; no stored generated/override two-field split).

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D2 (refined 2026-05-26), ADR-016 D4, ADR-007 D2, ADR-003, ADR-008 D1.

## Harness target
Signal: pytest — create a `PlatformConnection`, author an Event, assert eager-created projections FK to the connection (not a string) and carry default `provenance`; migration applies clean on an empty DB. Expected-green: projection.connection resolves to a PlatformConnection; provenance/generated_by/last_generated_at columns present; no `platform_id` field remains. Rationale: the schema refront is the load-bearing change C3/C5 and the adapters depend on; a model-level test is the goal-faithful altitude (a view test would pass even with the string FK still present). Invalidation: ADR-016 D4 connection field set changes.

## Origin
Discovered-from kb-a4u.1 during C3/C5 authoring-UX brainstorm convergence (2026-05-26). Blocks kb-a4u.3, kb-a4u.5, and the adapter beads that store per-organizer credentials.
acceptance_criteria: PlatformConnection model exists (organizer FK, platform, destination id, credentials, enabled flag, supported kinds). PlatformProjection.connection is an FK to PlatformConnection and platform_id string is removed. PlatformProjection has provenance enum (rule_template/agent_supplied/manual), generated_by (nullable), last_generated_at (nullable). Migration applies clean on empty DB. Existing override_data retained.

title: German translations never compiled in prod build — .mo missing at runtime
description: locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/django.mo is gitignored (only django.po is tracked). The Dockerfile installs gettext (line 32) but never runs 'manage.py compilemessages', and neither entrypoint.sh nor bin/init.sh do either. Result: the production image has no compiled German catalog, so Django falls back to the English msgid for every {% trans %} string when LANGUAGE_CODE/Accept-Language is German — German UI is effectively broken in prod despite the DE .po being maintained (CI even gates on the .po being non-empty). Discovered while greening the takedown DE translation tests (kb-cyp session 2026-05-26); fixed in CI test.yml by adding a compilemessages step before pytest, but the prod build path was left untouched (deferred to avoid touching the deploy pipeline mid-session).
design: Add 'manage.py compilemessages' to the Docker build (after COPY of source, gettext already installed at Dockerfile:32) so the .mo lands in the image layer shared across init/app/qcluster/bot — same rationale as collectstatic-at-build-time per kb-cm5. Do NOT put it only in init.sh: init is a separate container whose filesystem writes never reach the app container (the kb-cm5 collectstatic lesson). Verify post-deploy: request a page with Accept-Language: de and assert a known German string renders.
acceptance_criteria: Production image contains locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/django.mo; a German-locale request to /takedown/ renders 'Inhalt melden' (not 'Report content'). compilemessages runs at image build, not runtime-init-only.

There is no semi_public projection RESTRICTION to build — the platform does not box in facilitators. See ADR-016 revised carried-forward ADR-012 clause. notes:
## ADR-016 evolution alignment (2026-05-26)
D5/D6: the dogfooding cycle must EXPLICITLY emit reusable, composable artifacts (scripts, skills, switch-cli commands) for the agent-driven workflow — that is a stated goal, not a side-effect. The six per-adapter end-states now include explicit publish-lifecycle status (draft/ready/published/failed) and actor attestation: push-API platforms auto-confirm; FetLife reaches published via agent/human mark-published. title: C15 Guard: syndication is NOT gated by visibility tier (unlisted/semi_public still syndicate)
design:
REPURPOSED 2026-05-26 (C3/C5 brainstorm): the original "visibility-tier projection gating" premise (unlisted→0, public→all) is GONE — syndication is visibility-tier-agnostic (ADR-016 revised carried-forward ADR-012 clause; C4 write-gate removed). This bead becomes an inverted regression guard at the integration altitude: assert that visibility tier does NOT suppress syndication anywhere in the pipeline.

The guard verifies, end-to-end across the adapters, that an `unlisted` event (and a `semi_public` event) still eager-creates draft projections for every enabled connection and can be advanced/published exactly like a `public` event — i.e. no adapter, generation step, or eager-creation path silently re-introduces a visibility gate. Read-side `visible_to` on switch.berlin is unaffected and out of scope here (that is ADR-012 read-side rendering, not syndication).

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D4/D5 + revised carried-forward ADR-012 clause (visibility does NOT gate syndication); ADR-012 (read-side only, orthogonal).

## Harness target
Signal: pytest integration test across enabled connections. Expected-green: an `unlisted` event and a `semi_public` event each eager-create the SAME draft projection set as a `public` event (one per enabled connection × supported kind), and each can reach `ready`/`published` with no tier-based suppression at any adapter or generation step. Rationale: guards against regression to a visibility gate — the failure mode is a future dev re-adding `if event.visibility == unlisted: skip` somewhere in the pipeline; this asserts the inverse. Invalidation: the visibility-syndication-agnostic decision is reversed (would itself route through /adr-write).

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1; repurposed from gating-test to inverted-guard 2026-05-26 after the visibility-tier-gating decision was reversed (kb-wrb dissolved).
acceptance_criteria: An unlisted event and a semi_public event each eager-create the same draft projection set as a public event (one per enabled connection x supported kind) and can reach ready/published with no tier-based suppression at any generation step or adapter. Read-side visible_to on switch.berlin is unaffected.
notes:
## ADR-016 evolution alignment (2026-05-26)
Mostly unaffected — visibility gating remains a write-side (generation consults Event.visibility) assertion. D4 note: the projections this test counts now FK to PlatformConnections and are eager-created per enabled connection x supported kind. title: C5 Projection-review web UI: list, override-edit, status-flip, copy-to-clipboard
design:
Depends on C3 (review UI navigates from the authored Event/Post and extends `syndication/urls.py` which C3 creates; resolves R1-F3 + R1-F5 urls.py overlap by serializing after C3) and C4 (generation + status).

## Projection-review UX/IA (decided — C3/C5 brainstorm 2026-05-26; supersedes the prior design-first FLAG)

**The review board is a PANEL on the Event page, not a separate destination.** It is the `event_syndication` fragment of the Event hub (see kb-a4u.3) — the organizer never navigates "to the projections section." It renders the syndication status board: one row per projection (= per enabled connection x supported kind, eager-created per ADR-016 D4).

**Board row shape:** `connection (platform · destination) · kind · status-chip · provenance-tag · effective-copy preview · [expand → edit]`.
- **status-chip:** draft / ready / published / failed (ADR-016 D5).
- **provenance-tag:** derived from `provenance` (ADR-016 D2) — "template" / "from agent" / "edited" — gives the generated-vs-human signal with NO version machinery.
- **expand → edit:** inline per-field override editing (`override_data`); for promotion rows that's effectively the body. Effective content = live canonical + overrides, so non-overridden fields track the Event automatically.

**Status lifecycle UX (ADR-016 D5):**
- **Approve (draft -> ready):** explicit action, gated on completeness; the "missing X" state is shown on incomplete rows (also the save-and-resume cue).
- **Publish (ready -> published):** EXPLICIT action — per-row AND a batch "publish all ready" — never auto-on-ready. For push-API platforms the publish action performs the push; for no-API platforms (FetLife) the publish action surfaces copy-to-clipboard + deep link, the actor posts out-of-band, then attests via `mark-published` (a co-equal API verb, not a UI-only button — an agent calls the same verb and can verify before attesting).
- **failed:** prominent chip + the platform's actual error reason on expand + a manual retry action (failed-push governed by FIRM ADR-008 D3/D4 — no silent failures).

**Empty / error states (the originally-flagged gap), priority order:**
1. **No connections configured (first-run):** board shows "Connect platforms in settings to start syndicating ->" rather than an empty/broken panel.
2. **No promo Posts yet:** "No promo posts yet" + the inline [Add promo message] CTA.
3. **Connection broken/expired** (e.g. revoked Telegram token): surfaced at BOTH settings and every affected projection row ("can't publish — Telegram needs reconnecting"). Fail loud per ADR-008 D3.
4. **Seed/generation failure:** row shows "couldn't generate — missing X", NOT a silently-blank body (ADR-008 D3 — no zero-fill). Doubles as the WIP indicator.
5. **Content-policy flag** (kb-o0j clean_for_platform): pre-publish warning on the row ("may contain terms FetLife/Telegram reject — review") rather than letting the push fail downstream.

Per the alpine-3.x lesson (bd memories): the board is swap-heavy (status flips, generate, edit) — each swapped partial needs its own `x-data` root or directives go inert; verify in a live browser, not just unit tests.

## Dependencies
Depends on kb-a4u.18 (PlatformConnection schema + provenance field the board surfaces), kb-a4u.3 (the Event hub it's a panel of), kb-a4u.4 (generation + status engine).

## canonical_refs

## Harness target
Signal: pytest status-flip + override-edit persist + provenance-tag render + mark-published verb + the five empty/error states + manual browser check (swap behavior + x-data). Expected-green: the board renders one row per eager-created projection with status/provenance, inline override-edit persists and flips provenance to manual, explicit publish + actor-attested mark-published work, and each empty/error state renders its specified affordance. Rationale: the board is the facilitator-facing control surface for projection lifecycle; the goal-faithful altitude is the rendered board + lifecycle actions (a model-only test misses the swap/x-data failure mode and the empty-state affordances). Invalidation: ADR-016 D2 override/provenance model or D5 lifecycle changes.

## Origin

acceptance_criteria: (a) Projection-review UI lists projections per Event/Post; (b) per-projection override-edit view editing shadowed fields; (c) status-flip controls (draft->ready->published per legal transitions); (d) copy-to-clipboard affordance per projection (used by FetLife always + TT outcome-c); (e) "Generate projection" button per Event/Post invoking rule_based generation; test: status-flip persists, override-edit persists, copy-to-clipboard present for manual-assisted adapters.

title: C4 PlatformProjection generation engine: state-machine + override + clean_for_platform + eager visibility-agnostic creation (rule_based & agent_assisted)
design:
Generic projection substrate that adapters (C9/C11/C13/C14) plug into. Carries the state-machine, the live-canonical + override_data content model, fail-loud policy, the mode parameter, the clean_for_platform seam, AND eager projection creation.

## Content model (ADR-016 D2, refined 2026-05-26)
Effective projection content = **live canonical (Event/Post fields) + per-field `override_data`** (absent key = use canonical). There is NO stored generated_body/override two-field split. Consequence for the override-independence behavior: a field that HAS been overridden is stable when the canonical changes (the override shadows it); a field NOT overridden TRACKS the canonical automatically. Generation sets `provenance` (`rule_template` for mode=rule_based, `agent_supplied` for mode=agent_assisted; flips to `manual` later on human edit per C5) and the ADR-003 reservation fields `generated_by` (nullable) + `last_generated_at`.

## Eager creation (ADR-016 D4)
Generation exposes a "create draft projections for this Event/Post across the organizer's enabled connections" capability that the C3 authoring flow invokes: per enabled `PlatformConnection` × the kinds it supports (Event→listing-capable, Post→promotion-capable), create a `draft` projection FK'd to the connection. Respects `connection.enabled`.

## Syndication is visibility-tier-agnostic (ADR-016 carried-forward, REVISED 2026-05-26)
There is **NO visibility write-gate.** `Event.visibility` (ADR-012) governs read-side rendering on switch.berlin (`visible_to`) only — it does NOT gate outbound syndication. Eager creation is **uniform across all visibility tiers** (unlisted/semi_public/public produce the same draft set); the facilitator controls where the event actually goes via explicit publish (D5). The prior "unlisted → no external projections" gate (former R1-F11 fold) is REMOVED — it conflated read-side Switch visibility with outbound syndication and boxed in facilitators. Switch's own-event-page listing remains governed by the normal read-side `visible_to` rendering (not a syndication gate).

## Generation modes
mode=rule_based (default) deterministically generates a template body from canonical Event/Post fields into `override_data` seed, NO agent required, provenance=rule_template. mode=agent_assisted accepts an agent-supplied body/override and stores it (v0 semantics — no in-Switch voice-learning model at v0 per parent --design; the agent does the voice work and POSTs the result), provenance=agent_supplied. Both modes covered by the harness. Template seed is one-time at creation, not a re-runnable regenerate (ADR-016 D2).

clean_for_platform(text, platform_id) -> str identity-stub seam at syndication/cleaning.py, called before body assembly (kb-o0j fills real rules later in place — soft dep, not blocking).

## Dependencies
Depends on kb-a4u.18 (PlatformConnection + provenance/attribution fields generation writes), kb-a4u.1 (base schema), kb-a4u.2 (API skeleton).

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D2 (refined), D4, D5; ADR-008 D2/D3/D4; ADR-011 D1; ADR-003 (reservation fields). ADR-012 is orthogonal (read-side visibility only; does NOT gate syndication per ADR-016 revised carried-forward note).

## Harness target
Signal: pytest on (1) state-machine legal/illegal transitions; (2a) override-independence — set an override on a field, mutate that canonical field, assert projection rendered output STABLE; (2b) live-tracking — mutate a NON-overridden canonical field, assert projection rendered output CHANGES to track it; (3) mode=rule_based template generation sets provenance=rule_template; (4) mode=agent_assisted accepts+stores agent body, provenance=agent_supplied; (5) eager creation is visibility-tier-AGNOSTIC — unlisted/semi_public/public Events each produce the SAME draft set (one per enabled connection x supported kind); no tier gating. Expected-green: all green. Rationale: this is the substrate every adapter depends on; the 2a/2b split is the goal-faithful test of the refined live-canonical+override model; item (5) is a guard preventing regression to a tier-gate. Invalidation: ADR-016 D2 content model changes.

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1; content model + eager-creation aligned to ADR-016 D2/D4/D5 evolution 2026-05-26; visibility write-gate REMOVED 2026-05-26 (syndication visibility-agnostic per ADR-016 revised carried-forward).
acceptance_criteria: (a) Generation endpoint (POST) accepts mode=rule_based (default) | agent_assisted; rule_based produces a deterministic-template body from canonical Event/Post fields with NO agent; agent_assisted accepts an agent-supplied body and stores it; (b) clean_for_platform(text, platform_id)->str identity-stub seam exists and is called before body assembly; (c) status state-machine draft->ready->published->failed with legal-transition set enforced; failed-push fails loud per ADR-008 D4 (no silent retry on data-integrity; <=2 retries on transport then fail); (d) per-field override storage + apply (overrides shadow canonical values); (e) parent-acceptance-4 test: mutate a canonical field after generation, assert the projection rendered output (body from retrieval endpoint) is stable; (f) visibility write-gate: an unlisted Event generates NO external projections.
notes:
ENGINE CORE COMPLETE — commit ea6129c (2026-05-26). All 5 harness pytest checks green (27 tests in syndication/tests_engine.py; full suite 371 OK). Built: syndication/engine.py (generate_projection / render_projection / transition_status callables), syndication/cleaning.py (clean_for_platform identity stub seam). Override-independence via snapshot-into-override_data["body"] at generation time. Visibility write-gate blocks only `unlisted` (semi_public deferred to kb-wrb per scope-out). State-machine draft->ready->published->failed + failed->draft retry path; fail-loud per ADR-008 D4.

REMAINING (blocked on C2 = kb-a4u.2, the Django Ninja skeleton / open ADR decision): the HTTP generation POST endpoint + retrieval endpoint named in acceptance (a)/(e). The engine is a pure callable that C2's Ninja route and C7's CLI both wrap (co-equal-API per ADR-016 D3). Dep C4->C2 added 2026-05-26 to track this. title: C3 Event + Post CRUD endpoints + web UI authoring forms
design:
Core scope per ADR-011 D1 (must have web-UI affordance). Form precedents: organizers/forms.py, accounts/forms.py. No events/forms.py exists today. C3 creates `syndication/urls.py` (C5 later extends it — serial via the C3->C5 edge).

## Authoring UX/IA (decided — C3/C5 brainstorm 2026-05-26; supersedes the prior design-first FLAG)

**Mental model: Event-centric hub.** The organizer's primary object is the Event. The Event detail/edit page IS the single syndication hub — authoring, posts, and the projection-review board (C5) all live here; there is no separate "campaign composer" object and no separate "projections" destination. The one property worth borrowing from a campaign-composer UI — visibility of "what's going where" — is delivered by the on-page syndication board (C5), not by a new object.

**Fragment-seam composition (cheap foresight per ADR-003, within ADR-008 D2).** The hub page is a composition of independently-addressable, HTMX-swappable django_cotton components, each backed by its own endpoint and named by domain concept (`event_facts`, `event_posts`, `event_syndication`), NOT by layout position. The hub template composes them; it does not inline their query logic. This is correct HTMX hygiene anyway (status chips flip, projections regenerate, posts get added — all swaps), AND it makes a future reorg (e.g. promoting Posts to its own tab) a route+nav change, not a re-plumb. Do NOT build the tab/framework now (that would be ADR-008 D2 speculation). Per the alpine-3.x lesson (bd memories): each HTMX-swapped partial needs its own `x-data` root or directives go inert.

**Promo Posts are an inline add**, not a nav destination: an "Add promo message" action on the Event page creates a Post (+ eager promotion projections per D4). Keeps Posts feeling like an add-on to the Event.

**Connections + defaults settings surface.** C3 includes the organizer-facing UI to manage `PlatformConnection`s (per ADR-016 D4, schema from kb-a4u.18): connect a destination (Telegram channel, FetLife account, Ticket Tailor account; Switch own-page needs nothing), set per-destination credentials, toggle the `enabled` default. "Enabled" mostly means "connected." This is both the syndication-targets setting and the credential store the adapters consume.

**Save-always; completeness gated at draft->ready (ADR-016 D5).** Saving an incomplete Event is always allowed (it sits in `draft`); completeness is enforced at the `draft -> ready` transition, never at save. The fail-loud "missing X" state (ADR-008 D3) doubles as the save-and-resume affordance.

**Eager projection creation (ADR-016 D4):** authoring an Event eager-creates draft listing projections for each enabled listing-capable connection; authoring a Post eager-creates draft promotion projections for each enabled promotion-capable connection.

**Authorization (ADR-017 — supersedes the prior R1-F7 "no edit-gate" note):** authoring populates EventOrganizer + EventFacilitator through-tables (ADR-007 D2). Edit/publish is gated through the `can_edit`/`can_publish` seam (ADR-017 D2): a principal may edit iff they are a claimant of an `EventOrganizer` Profile of the Event (ADR-017 D1); `EventFacilitator`s are credited-only. The gate EXISTS in v0 — it is the predicate — and is trivially satisfied for the single-facilitator case (one organizer Profile, one claimant). This REPLACES the earlier "v0 ships co-host rows WITHOUT an edit-permission gate / deferred to follow-up bead F-authz" framing: co-*organizers* DO get edit via D1, and the F-authz follow-up was canonicalized as ADR-017 (kb-7oz, closed). C3 routes its edit/publish checks through the seam rather than inlining an `is_primary` check.

**Co-equal API (ADR-016 D3):** the authoring forms are HTML clients of the same logic the JSON API exposes; the web form submission and an agent's API call resolve to the same persistence (the HTML-vs-JSON-over-shared-logic mechanism is C2/kb-a4u.2's architecture call).

## Dependencies
Depends on kb-a4u.18 (PlatformConnection schema + projection FK refront + provenance/attribution fields). Depends on kb-a4u.1 (base schema), kb-a4u.2 (API skeleton).

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D1, D2, D3, D4, D5; ADR-017 D1, D2; ADR-011 D1; ADR-004; ADR-007 D2; ADR-003; ADR-008 D2, D3.

## Harness target
Signal: pytest form-submission persists all fields + manual browser check of the authoring hub page (UX). Expected-green: round-trip Event + Post via web UI persisting all ADR-016 D1 fields, with the Event page composing the event_facts / event_posts / event_syndication fragments and eager-creating draft projections per enabled connection. Rationale: core authoring is the wedge entry-point; the hub-composition + eager-creation is the goal-faithful behavior (a bare form test would miss the fragment seam and the eager fan-out). Invalidation: ADR-016 D1 field set or D4 eager-creation policy changes.

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1; authoring-UX IA decided in C3/C5 brainstorm 2026-05-26. Authorization paragraph corrected 2026-05-27 to reflect ADR-017 (the bead's prior "no edit-gate" note was superseded by ADR-017 lines 98/122).
acceptance_criteria: (a) Event CRUD endpoints (create/read/update/list/detail) backed by C2 skeleton; (b) Post CRUD endpoints scoped to an Event; (c) web UI Event authoring form carrying ALL ADR-016 D1 fields (parent acceptance 1 field list), HTMX+Alpine per ADR-004, populating EventOrganizer + EventFacilitator through-tables; (d) web UI Post authoring form scoped to an Event; (e) test: an Event authored via the web form persists all fields, and a Post authored persists with FK to Event. (Note: Post-authoring-via-agent-API path is satisfied here, not by C2 whose endpoints are stubbed.)
notes:
## Authorization resolved — ADR-017 (2026-05-26)
The prior 'co-host rows WITHOUT an edit-permission gate / policy deferred to F-authz' note is SUPERSEDED. ADR-017 D1: edit/publish authority = claimant of an EventOrganizer Profile (+ paired agent); EventFacilitators are credited-only. The gate IS the single can_edit predicate (ADR-017 D2) — trivially satisfied for v0 single-facilitator, but co-organizers DO get edit by being listed. Route all edit/publish checks through that predicate, not inline is_primary/claimant checks. kb-7oz closed.

title: C2 HTTP API skeleton: Django Ninja + auth (Bearer->identity-token->verify-identity) + OpenAPI
design:
Decided (resolves R1-F10 + user-confirmed): API framework = **Django Ninja** (in-process, Django-routed callables → satisfies the co-equal-API same-handler/same-middleware constraint; auto OpenAPI at root nearly free; fits ADR-004 HTMX-not-SPA + ADR-008 D2). On pickup, route the framework choice through /adr-write (likely an in-place note on ADR-001 or a small new ADR; the API *contract* is ADR-016 D3, the *binding* is not yet canonical). Implement Moltbook auth chain mirroring the MagicLinkToken one-time-token envelope (organizers/models.py). Endpoint bodies for Event/Post/Projection are STUBBED here (filled by C3/C4) — this bead lands skeleton + auth + docs only.

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D3, ADR-001 D8, ADR-004, ADR-014 D1, ADR-008 D2.

## Harness target
Signal: pytest on auth-rejection/acceptance + `curl /api/docs` returns OpenAPI schema. Expected-green: protected endpoint 401 without token, 200 with token; OpenAPI served at root. Rationale: auth + contract surface every other API child builds on. Invalidation: ADR-016 D3 auth mechanism changes.

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Django Ninja installed + registered; (b) API mounted under /api/ with OpenAPI/JSON-schema docs served at the API root; (c) auth chain: agents/register returns a one-time Bearer API key (mirroring MagicLinkToken envelope), identity-token-exchange endpoint (Bearer->short-lived identity token), verify-identity endpoint; (d) auth middleware enforces identity-token on protected endpoints; (e) test: unauthenticated request to a protected endpoint is rejected, authenticated request passes. Event/Post/Projection endpoint bodies are stubbed (filled by C3/C4).
notes:
UPDATE 2026-05-26 (C3/C5 brainstorm convergence): the API-framework binding is now canonical — ADR-016 D6 (Django Ninja; django-bolt rejected for breaking the co-equal-handler constraint). No need to route through /adr-write at pickup; build against Django Ninja per D6, with handlers over a shared service layer the HTMX views also use (so the co-equal test kb-a4u.9 can assert identical persistence/auth).
## D6 phrasing correction (2026-05-26, post-adversarial-review)
The earlier note's 'django-bolt rejected for breaking the co-equal-handler constraint' overstates ADR-016 D3 (which says co-equal *clients of one API surface*, not 'same callable'). Corrected framing per revised ADR-016 D6: build against Django Ninja because its in-process handlers let the JSON API and HTMX views share a SINGLE auth + service layer; django-bolt's separate Rust server with its own auth splits that layer, reintroducing the two-surface drift D3 forbids. The co-equal test (kb-a4u.9) asserts identical persistence/auth through that shared layer.
